positions.title: EECS 485 IA and Lab Instructor
positions.description:
•	Facilitating and leading lab sections focused on environment setup, project support, and web system concepts for a group of 20 students and hosting biweekly office hours.
•	Teaching students how to use industry standard web development tools such as Python, React, and AWS, along with overhauling the course documentation for React tutorials.
•	Working with other instructors involved in the course to maintain and update the course project code and documentation on our staff GitHub repository.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
•	Maintained and updated Amazon’s EDI Integration for its Vendor Central service to support right-to-left languages such as Arabic. 
•	Resolved multiple issues relating to translation bugs and localization problems which resulted in a better customer experience for the Arabic version of the website.
•	Cooperated with my teammates in assisting them with their issues in order to meet our goals and deadlines to launch the Vendor Central service in the Egyptian market.

positions.title: EECS 376 IA and Lab Instructor
positions.description:
•	Teaching assistant for EECS 376 (Foundation of Computational Theory).
•	Facilitating and teaching lab sections for a group of 20 students and hosting biweekly office hours.
•	Working with other faculty involved in the course to write challenging and thought-provoking computational theory problems for exams and homework.

company.name: University of Michigan College of Engineering

positions.title: SLC Study Group Facilitator
positions.description:
• Study group facilitator for MATH 156 (Applied Calc II Honors) at the University of Michigan Science Learning Center. 
• Leading and facilitating a study group containing 13 students.

projects.title: Jordan Street Art
projects.description:
• Founded an open-source project to document and preserve the street art in Jordan by creating a website that records and displays the location and pictures of the murals.
• Developed the frontend using the React frontend framework utilizing functional components to display pictures of the murals on a virtual map using the MapGL API.
• Utilized Flask API and REST API to implement the backend system to handle data fetching and processing;
deployed the website using AWS which was followed by unprecedented local engagement of 5000 website interactions within the first week.
• Interacted with dozens of local artists and collaborating with two NGOs to obtain the data necessary to create an authentic virtual tour of Jordan’s many murals.
